extracted.intended_audience: health insurance issuers, state regulators, policy analysts, and stakeholders submitting comments on Affordable Care Act rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory changes and requests for comment concerning actuarial value (AV), maximum annual limitation on cost sharing (MOOP), de minimis ranges, and related cost-sharing parameters for individual-market metal-tier and catastrophic plans beginning PY 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize AV requirement over maximum annual limitation on cost sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain the AV requirement for metal-level plans as the more specific, operational statutory instruction and prioritize it over the generally applicable maximum annual limitation on cost sharing when the two cannot reasonably be satisfied simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: AV establishes precise quantitative benchmarks that define metal tiers and requires detailed plan-level calibration; the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing is a broad consumer protection ceiling. Statutory interpretation and history (including congressional treatment of employer deductible limits) support giving effect to AV to preserve distinct coverage tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an incremental, limited approach to permitting plans to exceed MOOP
rubrics_metrics.description: Any regulatory framework permitting plans to exceed the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing should be as limited as possible and implemented gradually, starting with bronze and catastrophic plans before considering higher metal tiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: The disparity in component trend rates is growing year-over-year; begin with PY 2027 changes for bronze and catastrophic plans and defer other metal-tier changes to future notice-and-comment rulemaking to avoid destabilizing premium tax credit benchmarks (e.g., second-lowest cost silver plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand bronze de minimis range (expanded bronze)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and continue the existing expansion of the bronze de minimis range (previously expanded to a maximum of 65 percent AV) to preserve bronze plan viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: Since 2018 expansion, a higher share of bronze plans are at the upper end of the permissible range. Expanded bronze plans with AV up to 65% are referred to as 'expanded bronze.' This change was used to preserve plan offerings while acknowledging limits of further expansions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap enrollee spending in AV Calculator (initial $1,000,000 then percentile caps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a cap on enrollee spending in the AV Calculator (initially $1,000,000; later capped at the 99.50th percentile of annual allowed amounts) to reduce distortion from very high-spending outliers in the standard population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect: Without the cap, AVs for bronze (and other metal) plans would be several percentage points higher, rendering many bronze plans non-viable. Concern: expanding the cap further reduces representativeness and may conflict with statutory AV determination; seeking comment on alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow individual-market bronze plans to exceed MOOP in $50 increments to achieve permissible AV (§156.136 proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: For plan years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2027, an issuer may offer individual-market bronze plans that utilize a cost-sharing design exceeding the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing by amounts in increments of $50 to achieve an AV within the standard bronze de minimis variation, calculated as described in §156.135.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal specifics: MOOP increments of $50; no strict dollar upper bound specified (issuers calculate amount to fit within the narrower bronze de minimis range); HHS seeks comment on whether to set an upper bound upon finalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precondition: issuer must also offer a compliant bronze plan in same service area
rubrics_metrics.description: An issuer may use the expanded MOOP flexibility for additional bronze plans only if it also offers at least one individual-market bronze plan in the same service area that does not exceed the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing and complies with §156.140.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Ensures consumer access to at least one bronze plan that meets statutory MOOP limits and signals good faith adherence to statute. HHS may revisit this precondition in future rulemaking as AV trends evolve; seeks comment on alternatives (e.g., allowing flexibility only when standard bronze plans would be non-viable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit bronze MOOP flexibility to the individual market
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed flexibility allowing bronze plans to exceed the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing would apply only in the individual market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Individual-market consumers (particularly non-APTC-eligible) may benefit from more plan choices with lower deductibles and premiums; HHS seeks comment on whether policy should also apply to small group market.

rubrics_metrics.name: State primary enforcement and HHS review in directly-enforced States
rubrics_metrics.description: States retain primary enforcement authority over AV standards for issuers; HHS would conduct reviews in States where HHS directly enforces ACA insurance market reform requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may determine that a particular bronze plan design unnecessarily exceeds the MOOP; HHS invites comments about enforcement of the proposed flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider consumer protection disclosures for high-MOOP bronze plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider imposing disclosure requirements to educate and notify consumers about individual-market bronze plans that have a MOOP exceeding the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing (e.g., in the Summary of Benefits and Coverage and on Exchange websites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational timing: Such changes are unlikely for PY 2027 due to coordination/consultation constraints; HHS seeks comment on disclosure content, feasibility, and other consumer protection measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not set a strict dollar upper bound by default; rely on AV compliance to limit MOOP
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal does not specify a strict dollar upper bound on how much an issuer could exceed the MOOP; instead, the plan's AV requirement under §156.140 would constrain allowable MOOP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on whether a strict upper bound should be set annually or in final regulation and on what that upper bound should be; stresses plan AV compliance is the operative limiter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek alternative AV Calculator adjustments approximating inclusion of high-cost enrollees
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider allowing an adjustment to the AV Calculator output that approximates what a plan's AV would be if measured without a spending cap (i.e., including highest-cost enrollees), or consider reducing/removing the spending cap in future AV Calculator releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits comment on methods to better align with standard actuarial practice and on how to include more high-cost enrollees without disrupting existing plans' metal tiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider allowing bronze plans to exceed MOOP only when otherwise non-viable
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider imposing a condition that bronze plans may exceed the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing only when a standard bronze plan (MOOP at maximum) is impossible to design (i.e., non-viable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS seeks comment on this alternative precondition and other possible eligibility requirements for using the higher MOOP flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment on operational effects (plan identity, crosswalking, cost-sharing variants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comments on whether higher-MOOP bronze plans would be considered the same plan under §157.106(e)(3)(iv), impacts on plan crosswalking, and whether flexibility should apply to cost-sharing variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS requests input on administrative and operational consequences of allowing multiple MOOP variants and on how to treat such variants for enrollment, reporting, and SHOP/FFEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise catastrophic plan cost-sharing to require no benefits until 130% of MOOP
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose amending §156.155(a)(3) to require catastrophic plans to provide no benefits for any plan year (except as provided in §156.155(a)(4),(b),(c)) until an amount equal to 130% of the maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, rounded down to the next lowest multiple of $50, beginning in 2027 (for PY 2027 example: $12,000 × 1.3 = $15,400).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: To preserve a meaningful difference between bronze and catastrophic plans and encourage healthier, non-subsidized enrollees to select catastrophic plans by enabling lower catastrophic premiums; HHS selected 130% as an estimate to yield a theoretical AV of ~55% but invites comments and alternative factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider phasing, alternate multipliers, or requiring at least one 100% MOOP catastrophic plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on whether to phase in the catastrophic MOOP multiplier over time, choose a different factor than 130%, or require issuers to offer at least one catastrophic plan at 100% of the MOOP as a precondition to offering plans at 130%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS reserves ability to finalize a different factor; also seeks comment on impacts to plan availability and consumer choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require PY 2027 catastrophic plans using higher limit and consider multi-year terms
rubrics_metrics.description: If finalized, all catastrophic plans an issuer wishes to offer for PY 2027 would be required to use the higher annual limitation on cost sharing; HHS also proposes allowing catastrophic plans multi-year terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational: invites comment on how multi-year terms and the higher limit would affect plan offerings and risk pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment on impacts to HHS risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comments on whether requiring catastrophic plans to provide no benefits until 130% of the MOOP would have impacts on HHS risk adjustment (risk score transfers/payments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS requests evidence and analysis from stakeholders on potential risk adjustment consequences of changing catastrophic plan cost-sharing parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider revising PAPI methodology to better reflect individual-market claims growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether the methodology for estimating the Premium Adjustment Percentage Index (PAPI) should be revised to more accurately reflect per capita claims cost growth in the individual health insurance market so the annual MOOP adjustment better tracks that population's claims experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: The MOOP index currently may not track individual-market claims growth, which contributes to the divergence between AV increases and the statutory MOOP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid changing EHB benchmark framework to address AV increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on changing the Essential Health Benefits (EHB) benchmark framework to reduce AV increases because AV measures issuer cost sharing on whatever EHB the plan covers, and statutory constraints limit defining EHB to accommodate AV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory note: Section 1302(b)(2)(A) requires EHB to equal scope of a typical employer plan across 10 categories; changing EHB to accommodate AV is extreme and unlikely to yield material benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid failing to trend the AV Calculator as an actuarially unsound fix
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject not trending the AV Calculator (i.e., freezing trend adjustments) because doing so would render the AV Calculator 'wholly inaccurate actuarially.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS considered but declined this approach; seeks comment on administrable regulatory alternatives, but emphasizes actuarial fidelity of AV Calculator is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit policy scope to preserve AV calculation integrity and metal-tier comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Any adopted policy changes should seek to preserve the integrity of AV calculations and comparability between coverage levels while minimizing deviation from statutory requirements and representativeness of the standard population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS recognizes temporary measures (caps, de minimis expansions) may be necessary but warns against permanent expansions that undermine AV fidelity; invites comment on alternatives that balance viability and statutory adherence.
